slides.notes: Two groups from the challenge. They want a reason they can read, and no black-box scores. No real user has tried it yet, so this describes the intended audience.

slides.title: Broadband Gap Finder in one sentence
slides.sentence: A map tool that ranks 1 km squares where people live with slow fixed broadband, so sales teams can choose fixed-wireless campaign areas without guessing from municipal averages.
slides.notes: Fixed wireless means a home router on the mobile network. The map asks three questions: where is fixed slow, is mobile strong nearby, and how sure are we?

slides.title: How it works

steps.title: Public data
steps.text: Ookla speed tests joined to the 1 km population grid.

steps.title: Rules
steps.text: Slow under 30 Mbit/s; mobile 100 Mbit/s or more from 10 tests.

steps.title: AI rewords
steps.text: Gemini writes one sentence from the square's computed facts.

steps.title: Shortlist
steps.text: Sorted by residents × gap, exported with attribution.

callout.bold: Rules decide every label and rank.
callout.text: Code rejects any AI sentence whose numbers differ.

slides.notes: Tests are grouped into 1 kilometre squares and joined to population. Rules give each square a label, and the score only sorts. The AI only rewords, and code checks its numbers. These thresholds are my own choices and aren't confirmed with the mentor.

slides.title: What the 2026 Q3 data shows

bigStat.label: shortlisted squares passes every rule
bigStat.insight: 4 have unproven mobile; 15 rest on thin data: leads to check, not findings.

slides.notes: The honest result is that the data is thin. Of the 20 on the shortlist, 1 passes every rule, 4 have unproven mobile, and 15 are leads to check. The app shows that rather than hiding it.
